records.source: בַּשָּׁנָה֙ הָעֲשִׂירִ֔ית בָּעֲשִׂרִ֕י בִּשְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָ֥ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: In the tenth year, in the tenth [month], on [the] twelfth of the month, came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: In the tenth month of the tenth year, on its twelfth day, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.1: In the tenth year, in the tenth [month], on the twelfth of the month, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

R.1: On the twelfth day of the tenth month, in the tenth year of our exile, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

decisions.choice: the tenth year, the tenth month, the twelfth day: January 587 BC
decisions.reason: Counted from King Jehoiachin's exile in 597 BC (1:2), the date falls in January 587 BC (stated from general knowledge). Jerusalem had been under siege for a year (24:1-2), and an Egyptian army under Pharaoh Hophra had marched to relieve it and drawn the Babylonians away for a time (Jeremiah 37:5-11).

decisions.choice: chapters 29-32: seven oracles against Egypt
decisions.reason: Egypt receives the longest set of oracles among the nations. Six are dated (29:1; 29:17; 30:20; 31:1; 32:1; 32:17). They are in order of date except 29:17-21, the latest date in the book, placed here because it also concerns Egypt.

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me, saying (L); came to me (B); The LORD gave me this message (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula. Readable puts the day first and says what the years are counted from, as in 20:1.

records.heading: Pharaoh, the great monster of the Nile

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם שִׂ֣ים פָּנֶ֔יךָ עַל־פַּרְעֹ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְהִנָּבֵ֣א עָלָ֔יו וְעַל־מִצְרַ֖יִם כֻּלָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and prophesy against him and against Egypt, all of it.
pieces: Son of man, turn to face Pharaoh king of Egypt and prophesy against him and against the whole of Egypt.

L.2: Son of man, set your face toward Pharaoh king of Egypt, and prophesy against him and against Egypt, all of it.

R.2: Son of man, turn toward Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. Prophesy against him and against all of Egypt.

decisions.choice: son of man: a mortal, as God addresses Ezekiel
decisions.reason: See the note at 2:1.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh king of Egypt: Hophra
decisions.reason: Pharaoh was the title of Egypt's kings. The Pharaoh of Ezekiel's day was Hophra (Apries), who reigned about 589-570 BC (Jeremiah 44:30; stated from general knowledge). Zedekiah's hope of help from Egypt led to his revolt against Babylon (17:15-17).

decisions.choice: set your face toward (L); turn to face (B); turn toward (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording; see 6:2.

records.source: דַּבֵּ֨ר וְאָמַרְתָּ֜ כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה הִנְנִ֤י עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֔יִם הַתַּנִּים֙ הַגָּד֔וֹל הָרֹבֵ֖ץ בְּת֣וֹךְ יְאֹרָ֑יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָמַ֛ר לִ֥י יְאֹרִ֖י וַאֲנִ֥י עֲשִׂיתִֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Speak and say, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Look, I [am] against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great monster that lies in [the] midst of its streams, who has said, Mine [is] my Nile, and I, I made [it] for myself.
pieces: Speak and say, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great monster sprawling in the midst of its streams, who says, "The Nile is mine; I made it for myself."

L.3: Speak and say, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I [am] against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great monster lying in the midst of its streams, who has said, "Mine [is] my Nile, and I made [it] for myself."

R.3: Say to him, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I am against you, Pharaoh, king of Egypt. You are like a great monster lying in the middle of the streams of the Nile. You say, "The Nile is mine. I made it for myself."

decisions.choice: the great monster: the dragon of the waters, here like a crocodile of the Nile
decisions.reason: The word (*tannin*) names the monster of the sea that God overcame (Isaiah 27:1; 51:9; Psalm 74:13). Lying in the Nile it suggests the crocodile, Egypt's great beast. The Hebrew spells it like the word for jackals, but it is read as *tannin*, as in 32:2.

decisions.choice: the Nile and its streams: the river and its branches and canals
decisions.reason: Egypt lived by the Nile; in the delta it divides into branches, and canals carried its water to the fields. Pharaoh lies in them as if they were his own.

decisions.choice: my Nile ... I made it: Pharaoh claims to be its creator
decisions.reason: Egypt honored its king as a god. Like the ruler of Tyre (28:2), Pharaoh claims what belongs to God. The last words may also mean "I made myself".

decisions.choice: You are like a great monster
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture a comparison, so that young readers do not take Pharaoh for an animal, and names the Nile.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula. The LORD's words take no quotation marks; human speech quoted inside them takes double quotes.

records.source: וְנָתַתִּ֤י חַחִים֙ בִּלְחָיֶ֔יךָ וְהִדְבַּקְתִּ֥י דְגַת־יְאֹרֶ֖יךָ בְּקַשְׂקְשֹׂתֶ֑יךָ וְהַעֲלִיתִ֨יךָ֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ יְאֹרֶ֔יךָ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־דְּגַ֣ת יְאֹרֶ֔יךָ בְּקַשְׂקְשֹׂתֶ֖יךָ תִּדְבָּֽק׃
records.gloss: And I will put hooks in your jaws, and I will make [the] fish of your streams cling to your scales, and I will bring you up from [the] midst of your streams, and all [the] fish of your streams will cling to your scales.
pieces: I will put hooks in your jaws and make the fish of your streams stick to your scales. I will drag you up out of your streams, with all the fish of your streams clinging to your scales.

L.4: And I will put hooks in your jaws and make the fish of your streams cling to your scales, and I will bring you up from the midst of your streams, and all the fish of your streams to your scales will cling.

R.4: I will put hooks in your jaws and pull you out of the water. I will make the fish in your streams stick to your scales. All those fish will come out of the water with you, stuck to your scales.

decisions.choice: hooks in your jaws: the monster caught and dragged out
decisions.reason: The picture is of hunting a crocodile with hooks (Job 41:1-2). The same words are used of the lion in 19:4 and of Gog in 38:4.

decisions.choice: the fish of your streams: Egypt's people and those who depend on Pharaoh
decisions.reason: The fish that cling to the monster share its fate: the people, the troops and the allies who relied on Pharaoh.

records.source: וּנְטַשְׁתִּ֣יךָ הַמִּדְבָּ֗רָה אוֹתְךָ֙ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־דְּגַ֣ת יְאֹרֶ֔יךָ עַל־פְּנֵ֤י הַשָּׂדֶה֙ תִּפּ֔וֹל לֹ֥א תֵאָסֵ֖ף וְלֹ֣א תִקָּבֵ֑ץ לְחַיַּ֥ת הָאָ֛רֶץ וּלְע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם נְתַתִּ֥יךָ לְאָכְלָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will abandon you to the wilderness, you and all [the] fish of your streams; on [the] face of the field you will fall; you will not be gathered and not be collected; to [the] beasts of the earth and to [the] birds of the heavens I give you for food.
pieces: I will fling you into the desert, you and all the fish of your streams. On the open ground you will fall, and will not be gathered up or collected for burial. I will give you as food to the wild animals and the birds of the sky.

L.5: And I will abandon you to the wilderness, you and all the fish of your streams; on the face of the field you will fall; you will not be gathered up and you will not be collected; to the beast of the earth and to the bird of the heavens I give you for food.

R.5: I will throw you out into the desert, along with all the fish from your streams. You will fall on the open ground. No one will pick up your body or bury you. I will let the wild animals and the birds eat you.

decisions.choice: not gathered, food for beasts and birds: left unburied
decisions.reason: To lie unburied was the worst disgrace (Jeremiah 8:2; 22:19). A water monster thrown on dry land dies and rots in the open.

decisions.choice: not gathered and not collected: not taken up for burial
decisions.reason: The two verbs are used of gathering the dead for burial (Jeremiah 8:2). Some Hebrew manuscripts read "not buried" for the second (stated from general knowledge).

records.source: וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י מִצְרַ֔יִם כִּ֖י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה יַ֧עַן הֱיוֹתָ֛ם מִשְׁעֶ֥נֶת קָנֶ֖ה לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And will know all [the] inhabitants of Egypt that I [am] Yahweh, because they have been a staff of reed to [the] house of Israel.
pieces: Then all who live in Egypt will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. For the house of Israel they were a staff made of reed.

L.6: And all the inhabitants of Egypt will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because they were a staff of reed to the house of Israel.

R.6: Then everyone who lives in Egypt will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They have been like a walking stick made from a weak reed for the people of Israel.

decisions.choice: a staff of reed: a support that breaks
decisions.reason: The Assyrian commander used the same picture of Egypt a century earlier: a cracked reed that pierces the hand of anyone who leans on it (Isaiah 36:6; 2 Kings 18:21).

decisions.choice: and all the inhabitants of Egypt will know that I am the LORD (L); Then all the inhabitants of Egypt will know (B, R)
decisions.reason: The refrain follows the settled wording; see 6:7.

records.source: בְּתָפְשָׂ֨ם בְּךָ֤ בַכַּף֙ תֵּר֔וֹץ וּבָקַעְתָּ֥ לָהֶ֖ם כָּל־כָּתֵ֑ף וּבְהִֽשָּׁעֲנָ֤ם עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ תִּשָּׁבֵ֔ר וְהַעֲמַדְתָּ֥ לָהֶ֖ם כָּל־מָתְנָֽיִם׃ס
records.gloss: When they took hold of you by the hand, you broke and you tore for them every shoulder; and when they leaned on you, you broke and you made stand for them all hips.
pieces: When they grasped you in their hand, you splintered and tore open all their shoulders; when they leaned on you, you broke and wrenched all their hips.

L.7: When they took hold of you by the hand, you splintered and tore all their shoulders; and when they leaned on you, you broke and made all their hips stand [rigid].

R.7: When the Israelites took hold of you, you broke and cut their shoulders. When they leaned on you, you broke, and they hurt their backs.

decisions.choice: Egypt failed Judah when it leaned on it
decisions.reason: Judah's kings looked to Egypt against Assyria and Babylon (Isaiah 30:1-3; 31:1). Pharaoh Hophra's army withdrew and left Jerusalem to its fate (Jeremiah 37:5-8).

decisions.choice: you made all their hips stand rigid
alternatives: you made all their hips shake
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb means "make stand". Read with one letter changed, as several ancient translations seem to have read it (stated from general knowledge), it gives "you made all their hips shake". The Hebrew is kept, with the sense that the hips were wrenched stiff.

decisions.choice: the Israelites
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are.

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֛י מֵבִ֥יא עָלַ֖יִךְ חָ֑רֶב וְהִכְרַתִּ֥י מִמֵּ֖ךְ אָדָ֥ם וּבְהֵמָֽה׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Look, I [am] about to bring upon you a sword, and I will cut off from you human and beast.
pieces: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am bringing a sword against you, and I will cut off from you both people and animals.

L.8: Therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I am bringing a sword upon you, and I will cut off from you human and beast.

R.8: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I will bring war on you. I will kill your people and your animals.

decisions.choice: a sword: war, invasion
decisions.reason: The sword stands for an enemy army; 30:10-11 names Babylon.

decisions.choice: human and beast (L); both people and animals (B); your people and your animals (R)
decisions.reason: The wording follows 14:13 and 25:13. Readable says "war" for the sword.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula. The LORD's words take no quotation marks; human speech quoted inside them takes double quotes.

records.heading: Egypt laid waste

records.source: וְהָיְתָ֤ה אֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ לִשְׁמָמָ֣ה וְחָרְבָּ֔ה וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה יַ֧עַן אָמַ֛ר יְאֹ֥ר לִ֖י וַאֲנִ֥י עָשִֽׂיתִי׃
records.gloss: And will become [the] land of Egypt a desolation and a ruin, and they will know that I [am] Yahweh; because he said, The Nile [is] mine, and I, I made [it],
pieces: The land of Egypt will become a desolate ruin. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Because Pharaoh said, "The Nile is mine; I made it,"

L.9: And the land of Egypt will become a desolation and a ruin, and they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; because he said, "The Nile [is] mine, and I [am the one who] made [it],"

R.9: Egypt will become an empty ruin. Then the people will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Pharaoh said, "The Nile is mine. I made it."

decisions.choice: because he said, The Nile is mine: the boast of verse 3
decisions.reason: The charge is repeated, now spoken of Pharaoh rather than to him, before the sentence in verse 10.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker, since the Hebrew says only "he".

decisions.choice: and they will know that I am the LORD (L); Then they will know (B, R)
decisions.reason: The refrain follows the settled wording; see 6:7.

records.source: לָכֵ֛ן הִנְנִ֥י אֵלֶ֖יךָ וְאֶל־יְאֹרֶ֑יךָ וְנָתַתִּ֞י אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֗יִם לְחָרְבוֹת֙ חֹ֣רֶב שְׁמָמָ֔ה מִמִּגְדֹּ֥ל סְוֵנֵ֖ה וְעַד־גְּב֥וּל כּֽוּשׁ׃
records.gloss: therefore, look, I [am] against you and against your streams, and I will make the land of Egypt ruins of waste, a desolation, from Migdol [to] Syene, and to [the] border of Cush.
pieces: therefore I am against you and against your streams. I will make the land of Egypt a wasteland of ruins and desolation, from Migdol to Syene and on to the border of Cush.

L.10: therefore, look, I [am] against you and against your streams, and I will make the land of Egypt ruins of waste, a desolation, from Migdol [to] Syene, and up to the border of Cush.

R.10: So I am against you and against your streams. I will make the land of Egypt an empty ruin, from Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south, as far as the border of Cush.

decisions.choice: from Migdol to Syene, as far as the border of Cush: the whole length of Egypt
decisions.reason: Migdol was a fortress town in the northeast of the delta (Jeremiah 44:1). Syene is Aswan, at the first cataract of the Nile, Egypt's southern frontier. Beyond it lay Cush, the land of the upper Nile, in what is now Sudan.

decisions.choice: Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south
decisions.reason: Readable gives Syene its modern name and says where the places lie.

records.source: לֹ֤א תַעֲבָר־בָּהּ֙ רֶ֣גֶל אָדָ֔ם וְרֶ֥גֶל בְּהֵמָ֖ה לֹ֣א תַעֲבָר־בָּ֑הּ וְלֹ֥א תֵשֵׁ֖ב אַרְבָּעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: Not will pass through it [the] foot of human, and [the] foot of beast not will pass through it, and not it will be inhabited forty years.
pieces: No human foot will pass through it, and no animal's foot will cross it; it will stay uninhabited for forty years.

L.11: The foot of a human will not pass through it, and the foot of a beast will not pass through it, and it will not be inhabited forty years.

R.11: No people or animals will walk through it. No one will live there for forty years.

decisions.choice: forty years: a full period of judgment
decisions.reason: Forty years is a generation, the time of Israel's wandering in the desert (Numbers 14:33-34), and the number Ezekiel used for Judah's punishment (4:6). No record tells of Egypt standing empty for forty years; the number marks a whole period of judgment rather than a count of years. Nebuchadrezzar did invade Egypt in about 568 BC (stated from general knowledge; see verse 19).

records.source: וְנָתַתִּ֣י אֶת־אֶרֶץ֩ מִצְרַ֨יִם שְׁמָמָ֜ה בְּת֣וֹךְ׀אֲרָצ֣וֹת נְשַׁמּ֗וֹת וְעָרֶ֨יהָ֙ בְּת֨וֹךְ עָרִ֤ים מָֽחֳרָבוֹת֙ תִּֽהְיֶ֣יןָ שְׁמָמָ֔ה אַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַהֲפִצֹתִ֤י אֶת־מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם וְֽזֵרִיתִ֖ים בָּאֲרָצֽוֹת׃פ
records.gloss: And I will make [the] land of Egypt a desolation in [the] midst of lands made desolate, and its cities in [the] midst of cities laid waste will be a desolation forty years; and I will scatter Egypt among [the] nations and disperse them among [the] lands.
pieces: I will make the land of Egypt desolate among desolate lands, and its cities will lie desolate among ruined cities for forty years. I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them among the lands.

L.12: And I will make the land of Egypt a desolation amid lands made desolate, and its cities in the midst of ruined cities will be a desolation forty years; and I will scatter Egypt among the nations and disperse them among the lands.

R.12: Egypt will be an empty land among other empty lands. Its cities will lie in ruins among other ruined cities for forty years. I will scatter the people of Egypt among the nations and send them off to other countries.

decisions.choice: scatter among the nations, disperse among the lands: Israel's own judgment
decisions.reason: These are the words used of Israel's exile (12:15; 20:23; 22:15). Egypt, which failed Judah, will share its fate.

decisions.choice: the Egyptians (B); the people of Egypt (R)
decisions.reason: The verse speaks of the people, so Balanced and Readable say so; Literal keeps "Egypt".

records.source: כִּ֛י כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה מִקֵּ֞ץ אַרְבָּעִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ אֲקַבֵּ֣ץ אֶת־מִצְרַ֔יִם מִן־הָעַמִּ֖ים אֲשֶׁר־נָפֹ֥צוּ שָֽׁמָּה׃
records.gloss: For thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: At [the] end of forty years I will gather Egypt from the peoples where they were scattered there,
pieces: For the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: When forty years are over, I will gather the Egyptians from the peoples among whom they were scattered.

L.13: For thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: At the end of forty years I will gather Egypt from the peoples where they were scattered,

R.13: But this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: After forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the nations where they were scattered.

decisions.choice: after the judgment, a return
decisions.reason: As for Moab, Ammon and Elam (Jeremiah 46:26; 48:47; 49:6, 39), the LORD's judgment on Egypt is not his last word; Isaiah 19:22 also speaks of Egypt struck and healed.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula. The LORD's words take no quotation marks; human speech quoted inside them takes double quotes.

records.heading: A lowly kingdom

records.source: וְשַׁבְתִּי֙ אֶת־שְׁב֣וּת מִצְרַ֔יִם וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֤י אֹתָם֙ אֶ֣רֶץ פַּתְר֔וֹס עַל־אֶ֖רֶץ מְכֽוּרָתָ֑ם וְהָ֥יוּ שָׁ֖ם מַמְלָכָ֥ה שְׁפָלָֽה׃
records.gloss: and I will restore the fortunes of Egypt, and I will bring them back [to the] land of Pathros, to [the] land of their origin, and they will be there a lowly kingdom.
pieces: I will restore the fortunes of Egypt and bring them back to Pathros, the land of their origin, and there they will be a lowly kingdom.

L.14: and I will restore the fortunes of Egypt and bring them back [to] the land of Pathros, to the land of their origin, and they will be there a lowly kingdom.

R.14: I will make things good again for Egypt. I will bring them back to Pathros, in southern Egypt, the land they came from. But there they will be a weak kingdom.

decisions.choice: Pathros: Upper Egypt, the south
decisions.reason: Pathros is the southern part of Egypt along the Nile valley (Isaiah 11:11; Jeremiah 44:1). Egyptian tradition placed the beginnings of the kingdom there (stated from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: restore the fortunes (L, B); make things good again (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *shuv shevut*.

records.source: מִן־הַמַּמְלָכוֹת֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה שְׁפָלָ֔ה וְלֹֽא־תִתְנַשֵּׂ֥א ע֖וֹד עַל־הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וְהִ֨מְעַטְתִּ֔ים לְבִלְתִּ֖י רְד֥וֹת בַּגּוֹיִֽם׃
records.gloss: More than the kingdoms it will be lowly, and not it will lift itself up again over the nations; and I will make them few so as not to rule over [the] nations.
pieces: It will be the lowliest of kingdoms and will never again raise itself above the nations. I will make them so small that they will not rule over other nations.

L.15: More than the kingdoms it will be lowly, and it will not lift itself up again over the nations; and I will make them few, so that they do not rule over the nations.

R.15: It will be the weakest of all kingdoms. It will never again think itself better than other nations. I will make Egypt so small that it will never again rule over other nations.

decisions.choice: Egypt never again an empire
decisions.reason: Egypt had ruled Canaan and beyond for long periods. After the Persian conquest of 525 BC it was ruled for most of its later history by foreign powers, Persians, Greeks and Romans (stated from general knowledge).

records.source: וְלֹ֣א יִֽהְיֶה־עוֹד֩ לְבֵ֨ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל לְמִבְטָח֙ מַזְכִּ֣יר עָוֺ֔ן בִּפְנוֹתָ֖ם אַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And not it will be again for [the] house of Israel an object of trust, bringing iniquity to remembrance, when they turn after them; and they will know that I [am the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: Egypt will never again be something the house of Israel trusts in. Instead it will remind them of their guilt in turning to Egypt for help. Then they will know that I am the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.16: And it will no longer be for the house of Israel an object of trust, bringing iniquity to remembrance, when they turn after them; and they will know that I [am] the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.16: The people of Israel will never again depend on Egypt. Egypt will remind them of how they sinned when they turned to it for help. Then they will know that I am the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: bringing iniquity to remembrance: trust in Egypt was sin
decisions.reason: To rely on Egypt instead of the LORD was unfaithfulness (Isaiah 30:1-3; 31:1). The phrase "bringing iniquity to remembrance" is also used in 21:28-29 and Numbers 5:15.

decisions.choice: iniquity (L); guilt (B); sinned (R)
decisions.reason: *'Awon* follows the Isaiah table.

decisions.choice: and they will know that I am the LORD (L); Then they will know (B, R)
decisions.reason: The refrain follows the settled wording; see 6:7. Here the refrain names "the Lord GOD".

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י בְּעֶשְׂרִ֤ים וָשֶׁ֨בַע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה בָּֽרִאשׁ֖וֹן בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָ֥ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And it was in [the] twenty-seventh year, in the first [month], on [the] first of the month, came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: In the first month of the twenty-seventh year, on its first day, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.17: And it came about in the twenty-seventh year, in the first [month], on the first of the month, [that] the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

R.17: On the first day of the first month, in the twenty-seventh year of our exile, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

decisions.choice: the twenty-seventh year, the first month, the first day: April 571 BC
decisions.reason: Counted from Jehoiachin's exile, the date falls in April 571 BC (stated from general knowledge). It is the latest date in the book, sixteen years after 29:1, and comes soon after Nebuchadrezzar's long siege of Tyre ended. It is placed here, out of order, because it is about Egypt.

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me, saying (L); came to me (B); The LORD gave me this message (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula. Readable puts the day first and says what the years are counted from, as in 20:1.

records.heading: Egypt as Nebuchadrezzar's wages

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּ֠בֶל הֶעֱבִ֨יד אֶת־חֵיל֜וֹ עֲבֹדָ֤ה גְדֹלָה֙ אֶל־צֹ֔ר כָּל־רֹ֣אשׁ מֻקְרָ֔ח וְכָל־כָּתֵ֖ף מְרוּטָ֑ה וְ֠שָׂכָר לֹא־הָ֨יָה ל֤וֹ וּלְחֵילוֹ֙ מִצֹּ֔ר עַל־הָעֲבֹדָ֖ה אֲשֶׁר־עָבַ֥ד עָלֶֽיהָ׃ס
records.gloss: Son of man, Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon made his army labor a great labor against Tyre; every head was made bald and every shoulder was rubbed bare; and wages there were not for him and for his army from Tyre for the labor which he labored against it.
pieces: Son of man, Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon drove his army to a hard campaign against Tyre. Every head was rubbed bald and every shoulder worn raw. Yet he and his army got nothing from Tyre for all the labor he spent against it.

L.18: Son of man, Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon made his army labor a great labor against Tyre; every head was made bald and every shoulder rubbed bare; yet there were no wages for him or for his army from Tyre for the labor that he labored against it.

R.18: Son of man, Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon made his army work very hard to attack Tyre. The soldiers carried loads until their heads were bald and the skin on their shoulders was rubbed raw. But neither the king nor his army got anything from Tyre to pay them for all that hard work.

decisions.choice: son of man: a mortal, as God addresses Ezekiel
decisions.reason: See the note at 2:1.

decisions.choice: the long siege of Tyre
decisions.reason: Nebuchadrezzar besieged Tyre for thirteen years, from about 585 to 572 BC, according to Josephus (stated from general knowledge; see 26:7). Heads rubbed bald and shoulders worn raw come from carrying earth and timber for the siege works. Tyre came to terms with Babylon in the end, but its wealth was not taken.

decisions.choice: no wages from Tyre: the book records how events turned out
decisions.reason: Chapter 26 spoke of Tyre plundered (26:12). Here the LORD says plainly that Nebuchadrezzar's army gained nothing from Tyre, and gives it Egypt instead. The book keeps both words side by side; it does not hide that the plunder of Tyre did not fall to Babylon.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the spelling the Hebrew of Ezekiel uses, as in 26:7. Readable says what the bald heads and raw shoulders came from (m2).

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֥י נֹתֵ֛ן לִנְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְנָשָׂ֨א הֲמֹנָ֜הּ וְשָׁלַ֤ל שְׁלָלָהּ֙ וּבָזַ֣ז בִּזָּ֔הּ וְהָיְתָ֥ה שָׂכָ֖ר לְחֵילֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Look, I [am] about to give to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon the land of Egypt, and he will carry off its abundance, and plunder its plunder, and take as spoil its spoil, and it will be wages for his army.
pieces: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am giving the land of Egypt to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon. He will carry off its wealth, plunder it and strip it of its spoil, and that will be the pay for his army.

L.19: Therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I am giving to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon the land of Egypt, and he will carry off its abundance and plunder its plunder and seize its spoil; and it will be the wages for his army.

R.19: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to give the land of Egypt to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon. He will carry away Egypt's riches. He will take everything valuable he finds. That will be the pay for his army.

decisions.choice: its abundance: its wealth
decisions.reason: The word (*hamon*) means a crowd or abundance, the bustle and riches of a great land. It runs through the oracles on Egypt (30:4, 10, 15; 31:2, 18; 32:12, 16, 18-32), where it is often Egypt's "hordes".

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar in Egypt
decisions.reason: A broken Babylonian inscription tells of a campaign by Nebuchadrezzar against Egypt in his thirty-seventh year, about 568 BC, in the reign of Amasis (stated from general knowledge). How far it reached is not known.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula. The LORD's words take no quotation marks; human speech quoted inside them takes double quotes.

records.heading: Pay for his army

records.source: פְּעֻלָּתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁר־עָ֣בַד בָּ֔הּ נָתַ֥תִּי ל֖וֹ אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֲשֶׁר֙ עָ֣שׂוּ לִ֔י נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ס
records.gloss: [As] his wages for which he labored I have given him the land of Egypt, because they acted for me, declaration of [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: I have given him the land of Egypt as his pay for the work he did, because they worked for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.20: [As] his wages for which he labored I have given him the land of Egypt, because they acted for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.20: I have given him the land of Egypt to pay him for his hard work, because his army was working for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: they acted for me: Babylon as the LORD's servant
decisions.reason: Jeremiah calls Nebuchadrezzar "my servant" (Jeremiah 25:9; 27:6). His army's labor against Tyre was the LORD's work, and the LORD pays its wages.

decisions.choice: declares the Lord GOD (L, B); says the Lord GOD (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *ne'um Adonai YHWH* in Ezekiel.

records.source: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא אַצְמִ֤יחַ קֶ֨רֶן֙ לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּלְךָ֛ אֶתֵּ֥ן פִּתְחֽוֹן־פֶּ֖ה בְּתוֹכָ֑ם וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: On that day I will make sprout a horn for [the] house of Israel, and to you I will give opening of [the] mouth in their midst; and they will know that I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: On that day I will make a horn sprout for the house of Israel, and among them I will open your mouth. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.21: In that day I will make a horn sprout for the house of Israel, and to you I will give an opening of the mouth in their midst; and they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.21: At that time I will make the people of Israel strong again. And I will let you speak freely among them. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: I will make a horn sprout: I will give Israel new strength
decisions.reason: A horn is a picture of strength and of a strong ruler (1 Samuel 2:10; Psalm 92:11). Psalm 132:17 uses the same words for a king of David's line, and some read the verse that way; here the promise is for the house of Israel.

decisions.choice: an opening of the mouth: Ezekiel free to speak
decisions.reason: Ezekiel had been made unable to speak except when the LORD gave him a message (3:26-27), until the news of Jerusalem's fall came (24:27; 33:22). When the word against Egypt comes true, the prophet will be shown to be right and will speak among his people with confidence.

decisions.choice: In that day (L); On that day (B); At that time (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *bayyom hahu*. Readable says what the horn means (m1).

decisions.choice: and they will know that I am the LORD (L); Then they will know (B, R)
decisions.reason: The refrain follows the settled wording; see 6:7.
